about: Udai Pratap Autonomous College is located in the north-western part of Varanasi on a campus spanning approximately 100 acres. According to its official history, it began as the Hewett Kshatriya High School founded by Late Rajarshi Udai Pratap Singh Ju Deo in 1909, was raised to an Intermediate College in 1921 and became a degree college in 1949 when it commenced undergraduate classes in Arts and Commerce. The College was the first in Uttar Pradesh to be conferred autonomy by UGC in July 1991. It is NAAC accredited with a CGPA of 3.16 at 'A' grade, with autonomy extended up to 2032-33 by UGC. The B.Sc.(Hons.) Agriculture programme is accredited by ICAR's NAEAB.

identityNotes: Founded by Rajarshi Udai Pratap Singh Ju Deo (Raja of Bhinaga). First college in U.P. to receive autonomy (1991). Offers PG programmes (M.A., M.Sc., M.Com., M.Sc. Agriculture) since 1970 and a range of diploma courses, per official history.
researchNotes: Fees and placements were not published in numeric form on the official pages verified (the college has a Placement Cell PDF but no verifiable package figures were extracted). This research did not use aggregator-reported figures (e.g., a widely cited '3.5 LPA median' given by CollegeDunia). Course list reflects only programmes documented on the official UG course and History pages.
